newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO rangebound, Chinese demand healthy.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO rangebound, Chinese demand healthy.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices on Thursday were expected to be quoted within Wednesday's range as traders cited increased Chinese enquiries.
Traders expected 180-cst supplies for October lifting from Singapore to be quoted between $115-$116 per tonne on a free-on-board basis.

Chinese bids were heard ranging between $122-$124 per tonne on a cost-and-freight basis to South China, traders said. But they said cargoes for delivery at end September and early October have been traded on floating basis although no levels were indicated.

A major oil company was said to be moving two Mideast cargoes by October to the Far East. Traders said one cargo will be loading from Bahrain. They said a Dutch trader was also heard to be bringing another Mideast cargo east but the trader said the cargo has already been committed.
Some Iranian supplies were also heard to be arriving by October, traders said.
They said Kuwait should have more supplies for export in the fourth quarter as weather turns cooler.
Traders were uncertain if a major oil company and a shosha bidding in the market on Wednesday will emerge to buy again on Thursday.
In the swaps market, October paper was discussed around a dollar higher at $116-$116.50 from Wednesday.
